finding.mail_provider.mx_unresolvable: {count} MX host(s) no longer resolve to any address ({hosts}): mail may be lost or hijacked
module.mail_provider.checks: Identifies the mail provider named by the MX records, spots a security gateway (Mimecast, Proofpoint, Barracuda…) and finds the real mailbox provider behind it using SPF, autodiscover and DKIM CNAMEs and DNS verification tokens.
module.mail_provider.fix:
Compare the detected provider (and the security gateway, if any, with its confidence level) with what you actually use. Any unexpected provider (former vendor, trial, forgotten service) needs investigating: who set it up, and for what?
MX host that no longer resolves: if the server still exists, recreate the A or AAAA record for its name; otherwise delete that MX record from the DNS zone (registrar or DNS host console). A free MX name can be taken over by a third party, who would then receive your mail.
After a migration (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, gateway), delete the old MX records and check that only the intended servers remain, with the right priorities: `dig +short MX example.com`.
If a security gateway (Mimecast, Proofpoint, Barracuda...) filters your mail: accept mail on the final server only from the gateway's addresses (inbound connector, firewall rule), otherwise an attacker can bypass the filter by targeting the server directly.
Remove from SPF and DNS the sending services and domain verification tokens (TXT records) of providers you have dropped: they still authorize senders you no longer control.
A domain that receives no mail: publish a null MX (`0 .`, RFC 7505), an SPF record `v=spf1 -all` and a DMARC policy `p=reject`.
Keep the list of mail dependencies up to date (who hosts, who administers, which contract) and run the scan again after every MX change.
module.mail_provider.fix_snippet:
# DNS MX
example.com.  IN  MX  10  mail.example.com.
# DNS null MX
example.com.  IN  MX  0  .
example.com.  IN  TXT  "v=spf1 -all"
_dmarc.example.com.  IN  TXT  "v=DMARC1; p=reject"
# dig
dig +short MX example.com
dig +short A mail.example.com
module.mail_provider.title: Mail provider
module.mail_provider.why: Knowing who really hosts the domain's mail tells you which controls matter (phishing, tenant configuration, dependencies) and reveals orphaned MX hosts a third party could take over.
